vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: Latin Ceret, Caeret, which has been etymologically identified with Caere in Etruria.
Through a modern Indian language from Sanskrit शिरीष (śirīṣa), which actually means Albizia lebbeck known as لَبَخ (labaḵ).
From Mašriqi dialects, from Aramaic שֻׁרְשׁא (šuršā) / ܫܪܫܐ (šeršā), from Proto-Semitic *šurš- (“root, wort”).
From coastal African dialects, from Latin circius.
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.
From Coptic *ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲱϣ (*petrōš, “the flamingo”), from Egyptian dšr. Also found metathesized as Tunisian Arabic شَبْرُوش (šabrūš, “flamingo”).

mana.dayanak_tanim: become settled or established and stable in one's residence or life style
